skill.name: design-style-skill
skill.description: Selects consistent PPT visual design styles with radius, spacing, typography, and component recipes for PptxGenJS slide work.
skill.summary: Guides PPT style selection with radius, spacing, typography, and component rules.
skill.author: MiniMax-AI

security_audit.summary: All four static external command alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code fences in SKILL.md. The skill provides PPT design style guidance and PptxGenJS shape examples; no evidence found of prompt injection, shell execution, network activity, or filesystem access.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 112 starts a JavaScript fenced example for PptxGenJS shape styling. The surrounding lines only set shape dimensions, fills, and rectRadius values, with no shell command execution.
Line 133 is the closing Markdown fence for the JavaScript example. It is not Ruby backtick execution and cannot run an external command.
Line 141 starts another JavaScript fenced example showing radius relationships between card and button styles. The content is static presentation design guidance, not executable shell logic.
Line 149 is the closing Markdown fence for a small style comparison block. There is no command invocation or user-controlled command construction.

content.value_statement: PPT decks often lose quality when radius, spacing, and component styles drift. This skill provides clear style recipes for consistent slide systems.
actual_capabilities: Recommends four PPT visual style recipes: Sharp, Soft, Rounded, and Pill.
Provides radius and spacing values in inches for 16:9 slides.
Maps buttons, cards, images, inputs, badges, and avatars to style-specific radius values.
Explains when to use compact, balanced, spacious, or airy layouts.
Gives typography and spacing ranges for common slide elements.
Shows PptxGenJS rectRadius examples for cards and buttons.
limitations: Does not generate complete PPTX files by itself.
Focuses on radius, spacing, and typography, not full brand systems.
Assumes PptxGenJS inch units and 10 by 5.625 inch 16:9 slides.
Requires user-provided brand colors, imagery, or content strategy when needed.

use_cases.title: Standardize Executive Decks
use_cases.description: Create a consistent visual system for reports, updates, and board presentations.

use_cases.title: Design Dense Data Slides
use_cases.description: Choose compact radius and spacing rules for tables, KPI cards, and financial dashboards.

use_cases.title: Shape Product Launch Stories
use_cases.description: Use spacious component styles for product messaging, marketing slides, and brand moments.

prompt_templates.title: Pick a Slide Style
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend one PPT visual style for a quarterly business update. Explain the radius, spacing, and typography choices in simple terms.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Component Tokens
prompt_templates.prompt: Define radius and spacing values for cards, badges, buttons, and image containers in a product launch deck.

prompt_templates.title: Balance Mixed Sections
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a style plan for a deck with dense data slides and spacious marketing slides. Keep component radius relationships consistent.

prompt_templates.title: Convert to PptxGenJS Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this presentation direction into PptxGenJS design rules for rectRadius, margins, section spacing, and type scale.

output_examples.input: A finance review deck with many tables and KPI cards.
output_examples.output: Recommended style: Sharp and Compact. Use small radii, tight spacing, narrow page margins, and restrained typography for high information density.

output_examples.input: A product launch deck needs a friendly modern look.
output_examples.output: Recommended style: Rounded and Spacious. Use larger radii, wider gaps, generous card padding, and medium-large headings.

output_examples.input: A brand keynote should feel open and premium.
output_examples.output: Recommended style: Pill and Airy. Use capsule buttons, wide margins, strong whitespace, and limited dense content per slide.

best_practices: Choose one primary style before creating component layouts.
Match spacing density to the slide purpose and information load.
Keep outer containers at least as rounded as inner controls.
anti_patterns: Mixing Sharp containers with Pill buttons without a clear hierarchy.
Using wide spacing on dense financial or table-heavy slides.
Applying large radii to small elements until shapes look distorted.

faq.question: What type of presentations does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports PPT decks that need consistent radius, spacing, typography, and component styling.

faq.question: Can it create a complete PowerPoint file?
faq.answer: No. It provides design rules that another workflow can apply when creating slides.

faq.question: Does it work with PptxGenJS?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance uses PptxGenJS inch units and includes rectRadius examples.

faq.question: Which style should I use for dense data?
faq.answer: Use Sharp and Compact or Soft and Balanced for tables, KPI cards, and financial reports.

faq.question: Which style should I use for marketing decks?
faq.answer: Use Rounded and Spacious or Pill and Airy for product introductions and brand presentations.

faq.question: Can I mix styles within one deck?
faq.answer: Yes, but keep radius hierarchy and spacing density consistent across related components.
